verdict.plain_language: The earlier reading FALLS. We reported that 40 of the 72 heads carry a negative MATCH_prev mixture coefficient and called that "suppression". A pattern coefficient's sign is not a behaviour: the patterns in this family are signed (no softmax) and the value-output path is signed too, so a negative coefficient times a negative value-output copy score is a POSITIVE push on the copied token. Three measurements now agree that the match family is, on net, PROMOTING copying. First, the reference ablation: deleting every head's match term at once collapses the induction advantage from 2.079 to 0.485 nats (change -1.593, standard error 0.038) and costs +1.647 nats of cross-entropy on the second copy -- the family as a whole is worth most of the model's induction, in the promoting direction. Second, weight space: of the 40 negative-coefficient heads, 28 (70%) also have a NEGATIVE composed copy score through their own decoder slot and the tied unembedding, so their composed effect is a double negative -- net attraction toward the copied token -- and only 12 are suppressive once composed. Third, causality: zeroing one head's coefficient at a time over the 12 largest-magnitude heads plus 4 small-magnitude controls, 5 of 16 heads move the induction advantage by more than 1% of the family effect. Every materially promoting head -- L1H3, L7H1, L1H0, L3H1, L1H4 -- has a NEGATIVE coefficient, and the largest single contributors are L1H3 (coefficient -2.86, copy score -2.45, advantage change -0.175); L7H1 (coefficient -1.62, copy score -14.87, advantage change -0.138); L1H0 (coefficient -3.02, copy score -0.64, advantage change -0.087). NO head is materially suppressive: the largest positive move is L6H4 at +0.013, below the 0.016 threshold, and it carries a positive coefficient anyway. The raw coefficient sign predicts the causal direction for only 0/5 of the materially-moving heads, while the composed weight-space sign gets 5/5; over all 16 probed heads (including the near-zero movers, where the sign is defined but meaningless) the numbers are 4/16 for the raw coefficient and 12/16 for the composed score. Correct statement: the predicate-basis model wires induction through heads whose match coefficient is negative and whose value-output copy path is also negative; the sign of the mixture weight alone carries no behavioural meaning and must never be reported as suppression without composing through the value-output path and checking causally. Robustness: replacing the embedding-only key representation by the model's actual block input at real key positions moves the weight-space count from 28 to 23 of 40 net-promoting -- the majority conclusion is unchanged, but the weight-space copy score is a screen, not the verdict; the causal ablation is. Magnitude calibration: 28 of 72 heads have a copy score above the 95th percentile of random decoder blocks at matched Frobenius norm (2.21), so these are real value-output alignments, not noise.
